title: The Man in Linen: Daniel 10-12, Job 22, John 13, Jude
summary: Daniel 10-12 was taught as one final vision in plain words (Henry paraphrased), dated to the third year of Cyrus (about 536 B.C.) when the rebuilding had stalled under opposition (Ezra 4:4-5), which Calvin gives as the cause of Daniel's three-week fast (it ran through Passover). The man in linen was left open (Henry and Hippolytus: Christ; Calvin: an angel) and promised for Revelation 1:13-15. The hard question, the prince of Persia (sar), was answered with Jerome (Persia's angel accusing Israel), Calvin (King Cambyses), Ligonier Tabletalk (a demon), and Piper's Ligonier article quoted (the twenty-one days match Daniel's fast; 'Daniel's praying was not about angels'); the host leaned angelic because sar also names Michael. Chapter 11 was walked through (Xerxes, Alexander, Ptolemies and Seleucids, Antiochus IV Epiphanes / Epimanes, the abomination of 167 B.C., 11:32 with Spurgeon No. 609 paraphrased on the Maccabees), Porphyry's late-date argument and Jerome's answer (paraphrased), and 11:36-45 as Antiochus becoming a type of the final enemy (Jerome: Antichrist; Calvin: Rome; host with Tabletalk). Daniel 12:2 was taught as the clearest Old Testament resurrection text: 'everlasting life' occurs only here in the Old Testament, dera'on only here and Isaiah 66:24, with Calvin and Jerome (against Porphyry) quoted and John 5:28-29 as the one NT move; 12:3 echoes Isaiah 53:11; 12:8 'I heard, but I did not understand'; the numbers held loosely; application from 12:13: Daniel gets a lot, not a chart, so go your way. Job 22 (Eliphaz's last speech, third cycle) covered the first specific (false) charges, Spurgeon's 1885 sermon paraphrased (virtue from prosperity, sin from adversity), 22:21 'agree with God' and 22:25 'the Almighty will be your gold' as unwittingly arguing Satan's case from 1:9, Gregory's Moralia 16 quoted ('words of knowledge in not knowing'), and the irony of 22:30 fulfilled in 42:8. John 13:31-38: 'now' after Judas leaves, glory five times, Calvin's cross as a theater (paraphrased), teknia, mandatum novum, Chrysostom Homily 72 quoted (new by the manner, 'Myself have begun'), Sproul quoted via Tabletalk ('a love that has no place for treason'), and Peter's vow with Augustine Tractate 66 paraphrased ('not you cannot, but you cannot now'). Jude 17-25 finished the book: remember the apostles (2 Peter 3:3), one imperative 'keep yourselves' with Piper quoted ('God is the one who keeps you in his love'), the three groups and Zechariah 3 (brand from the fire, filthy garments, 'The Lord rebuke you' as in Jude 9), and Spurgeon No. 2296 paraphrased on stumbling. The close tied Peter's failed vow to the God who is able to keep, the names in the book (Daniel 12:1), and everlasting life (Daniel 12:2; Jude 21).
threads: Daniel is finished. Hosea 1-3 begins next plan day (new book: compact introduction needed: Hosea son of Beeri, eighth century B.C. under Jeroboam II and the last kings of Israel, Gomer, Jezreel, Lo-ruhamah, Lo-ammi, 1:10 and 2:23 quoted in Romans 9:25-26 and 1 Peter 2:10, chapter 3 buying her back). Calvin's Commentary on Hosea (ccel calcom26) and Jerome's commentary on the Minor Prophets exist.

Revelation 1:1-8 begins next plan day (new book: compact introduction: John on Patmos, date about A.D. 95 under Domitian per Irenaeus, the seven churches, genre). Revelation 1:7 joins Daniel 7:13 and Zechariah 12:10. The episode promised that the man in linen of Daniel 10:5-6 returns in Revelation 1:13-15 (likely the following plan day, 1:9-20); Henry and Hippolytus read Daniel 10 as Christ, Calvin as an angel. Close that thread when Revelation 1:13-15 is read.

Job 23 is next: Job answers Eliphaz with 'Oh, that I knew where I might find him' (23:3), 'he knows the way that I take; when he has tried me, I shall come out as gold' (23:10, answering Eliphaz's 'the Almighty will be your gold' in 22:25), and 'I have treasured the words of his mouth' (23:12). Unused Job 22: Henry 'Methinks I can almost forgive Eliphaz' (devo only) and 'God rebukes the good because he loves them, but he never rebukes the great because he fears them'; Spurgeon 1885 'I suspect that Eliphaz and his friends had enjoyed smooth sailing' (devo only); Maclaren 'It pays to be religious'; Derek Thomas (Ligonier, 'With Friends Like These') 'It's karma'; Keil on the true premises and false conclusion; Spurgeon Morning and Evening May 8 evening on 22:21.

John 14:1-14 is next: 'Let not your hearts be troubled', 'In my Father's house are many rooms', Thomas's question and 'I am the way, and the truth, and the life', Philip and 'whoever has seen me has seen the Father', greater works, asking in his name. It answers Peter's 'Lord, where are you going?' (13:36). Augustine Tractates 67-71 and Chrysostom Homilies 73-74 cover it; Calvin's John continues at biblehub calvin/john/14.htm. Keller's 2016 'Jesus, Mission, and Glory' series continues. Unused 13:31-38: Augustine 'Will you do for me what I have not yet done for you?' and 'He saw what was the kind of desire in his mind; but what the measure of his strength, he saw not'; Calvin 'as if it had been a law but lately made' and 'fire and water'; Henry 'an old book in a new edition corrected and enlarged' and 'he seems to have said this with a smile'; Spurgeon No. 2936 on the 'eleventh commandment' (Rutherford story).

Jude is finished. Unused Jude 17-25: Calvin on psychikoi ('no part of us aspires to God, until we are renewed by his Spirit'), Calvin on 22 (meek and teachable vs hard and perverse); Henry 'his brother's keeper' and 'We must distinguish between the weak and the wilful'; Piper 'the older I get, the more I am amazed... that I am still a Christian'; Ligonier Tabletalk 'Now to Him' ('Those with true faith will not finally fall away'); Clement of Alexandria's Adumbrations on 23-24 (paraphrase only).

Unused Daniel 10-12: Spurgeon No. 1089 (1873) 'God's life! is not made up of tickings of the clock! He can wait, he can wait.' and 'great love from God will make you have great humbleness of soul'; Spurgeon Faith's Checkbook on 12:13 ('Calmly resolute in duty...', devo only); Calvin on 10:1 'If a promise should tarry, wait for it'; Calvin open to Michael as Christ; Henry 'One touch from heaven brings us to our knees', 'Truth is the daughter of time', 'to choose suffering rather than sin is a great exploit'; Jerome on 12:3 'it is not enough to know wisdom unless one also instructs others' and his 'bruised serpent' line on Porphyry; Hippolytus on the two men on the banks as the law and the prophets; Ligonier Tabletalk 'Michael, the Chief Prince' caution about binding territorial spirits; Ligon Duncan 'Blessed Is the One Who Waits' (fetched, unused).

Voices quoted this episode: John Piper (Ligonier article 'Prayer', Daniel 10; T4G 2012 on Jude), Jerome (Commentary on Daniel 12), John Calvin (Daniel 12:2), Gregory the Great (Moralia 16 on Job 22), John Chrysostom (Homily 72 on John), R. C. Sproul (via Ligonier Tabletalk 'A New Commandment from Christ'). Paraphrased: Henry, Hippolytus, Calvin (Daniel 10, John 13:31), Jerome (10:13 and Porphyry), Ligonier Tabletalk (2010, 2013), Spurgeon (Nos. 609, 2296, and 'Delight in the Almighty' 1885), Ellicott on Job 22:30, Augustine Tractate 66, Keller 'The True Disciple'. Desiring God still returns a Cloudflare challenge; Piper came via Ligonier and TGC.

show_notes: Daniel's last vision: a three-week fast, a man clothed in linen, the prince of Persia, the kings of the north and south, and the clearest resurrection promise in the Old Testament. Eliphaz says true things to the wrong man, Jesus gives the new commandment as Peter makes a vow he cannot keep, and Jude ends with the God who is able to keep you from stumbling.
